# Versatile / all-in-one lenses — can one lens do portrait + landscape?

**Dimension:** Canon-brand RF/RF-S zooms that combine landscape + portrait and
serve as a single travel lens. This directly answers the user's question: *can
some lenses be combined to do portraiture and landscape?* Sources in
[citations.md](../citations.md); terms in [glossary](../glossary.md).

## The short answer

**Yes — a 24–105 mm zoom covers both.** 24 mm is wide enough for landscapes and
travel scenes; 105 mm reaches flattering portrait territory. One lens spans the
useful range without swapping [[42]](../citations.md#c42). The tradeoff is
aperture (less background blur than a fast prime) and ultimate sharpness
[[27]](../citations.md#c27)[[49]](../citations.md#c49).

## Recommendation logic (portrait + landscape + travel in one)

- **Lightest do-everything on APS-C:** **RF-S 18-150mm** (~305 g) — 28.8–240 mm
  equiv covers wide scenics through portrait/short-tele in one light lens; the
  single best one-lens travel solution for an APS-C body
  [[46]](../citations.md#c46).
- **Lightweight full-frame:** **RF 24-105mm f/4-7.1 STM** (~395 g, ~$399) — wide
  to short-tele, very light and cheap; the f/7.1 long end limits background blur
  [[43]](../citations.md#c43).
- **Best-quality one-lens (heavier):** **RF 24-105mm f/4L** (700 g) — constant
  f/4, weather-sealed, sharper; the classic travel standard but adds weight
  [[42]](../citations.md#c42).
- **Maximum reach travel:** RF 24-240mm (750 g) trades some image quality for a
  10× range [[45]](../citations.md#c45).

## Counter-perspectives

- **One lens can't truly excel at both extremes:** landscapes want stopped-down
  corner sharpness + wide angle; portraits want wide aperture + longer reach. A
  zoom compromises both; Canon-forum users frame it as "more likely a 2-lens
  endeavor" for best results [[50]](../citations.md#c50).
- **Variable f/4-7.1 is slow for portraits:** by ~79 mm the STM zoom is well
  past f/4, so background separation at the long end is weaker than a prime or
  the f/4L [[43]](../citations.md#c43)[[42]](../citations.md#c42).
- **Superzoom image-quality cost:** the 24-240mm leans on in-camera corrections;
  RAW corners soften at the extremes [[45]](../citations.md#c45).
- **Primes still win on sharpness/aperture** — convenience vs absolute quality
  [[49]](../citations.md#c49).
- **RF-S lenses are APS-C-only** — if you later upgrade to full-frame, an RF-S
  zoom won't carry over as a full-frame solution [[46]](../citations.md#c46).

## Gaps and limitations

- The RF 24-105mm f/4-7.1 STM's claimed ~0.5× magnification (vs the f/4L's
  0.24×) came from one source and may use a different measurement convention —
  flagged for verification [[43]](../citations.md#c43).
- Weather-sealing of the RF 28-70mm f/2.8 IS STM ("plastic build") unconfirmed.
- Weights via review snippets; Canon spec pages were fetch-blocked.
